real_name: UNNAMED in film — points unmistakably to General Ashfaq Parvez Kayani, COAS Pakistan 2007-2013
real_life_notes: The film's most pointed accusation. When Major Iqbal confirms the 26/11 plot has the blessing of 'Bade Sahab' (Big Boss), he is referencing the authority that controls the entire military-terror nexus. In 2008 context, this is General Ashfaq Parvez Kayani — Chief of Army Staff (COAS) of Pakistan from 2007-2013. The film never names him, but the pointing is unmistakable given the explicit ISI-26/11 framing throughout.
film_role: Film 1 Act 3 — the unseen authority whose blessing Major Iqbal references when confirming the 26/11 attack is authorised. Represents the thesis that 26/11 was state-sponsored at the highest level of the Pakistani military establishment.
objective: Maintain Pakistan Army's strategic depth through proxy terror; ensure deniability; use non-state actors as an instrument of state policy against India
oracle_note: Bade Sahab is the highest-capability, highest-trigger-threshold actor in the entire network. The oracle treats him as an environmental constant — his existence sets the upper bound of the adversary system. He is not a direct target in either film but is the structural reason Major Iqbal can operate with impunity.
real_status: General Kayani retired 2013. No public accountability for 26/11. India has formally requested his questioning; Pakistan has denied all such requests.
directorial_choice: Aditya Dhar deliberately does not name him — this maintains legal deniability while ensuring the audience understands the implication. It is the film's most politically loaded choice.
loss_aversion_note: λ=1.2, near risk-neutral. Institutional actors at this level treat threats as manageable variables, not personal losses. Extremely difficult to deter through cost-imposition — institutional continuity transcends individual outcomes.
